text:
Maya L: :rotating_light: FYI we started seeing a spike in provisioning failures from apac-gpu-rack-03 after the scheduled BIOS push at 03:00 UTC
Infra Bot: deploy-bot applied bios-image v1.12 to rack-apac-3 at 2026-03-18T03:00:12Z
Tony H: Symptoms: nodes fail PXE/serial provisioning, OOB SOL intermittently disconnects, and some BMCs report secure-boot state toggled to 'enabled' with unknown key hash
Leo: Checked the canary — weirdly it came up but was marked untrusted in the inventory because the EFI signature GUID differs from last known signing key
Sara: Provisioning queue spiked to ~120 pending GPU nodes once Dedicated autoscaler retried requests. Cost estimate shows a ~15% uplift in burst spend for the last 2 hours
Oncall Eng: Did we hit the runbook for secureboot key drift?
Maya L: Yes, I tried the quick-check: `ipmitool -I lanplus -H bmc-host -U admin -P **** fru print`
Maya L: Also pulled the BMC logs: `journalctl -u bmc | grep -i secureboot` — shows EFI_VARIABLE update and then a key mismatch event
Tony H: TPM PCRs look normal. This is not a TPM throw — it's an image signing key rotation on the BIOS that added a new default cert and flipped the secureboot flag in some units
Leo: Quick workaround: set the machine's boot policy to allow unsigned images temporarily and re-provision, then re-lock secureboot after >canary verification. But that's risky for compliance customers
Sara: Compliance is a concern for a subset of Dedicated customers. We need a non-manual path. Can we automate a key import via the BMC for the new cert? Any IPMI/Redfish command to upload platform keys?
Tony H: Redfish supports Key Exchange Key (KEK) and db updates: `PATCH /redfish/v1/Systems/1/SecureBoot` with payload to update keys. But BMC vendors differ — some units accept the request, others reject with 400
Oncall Eng: For immediate stabilization I suggest: 1) Pause autoscaler burst in apac region, 2) Suspend blue/green provisioning for rack-apac-3, 3) Move queued jobs to eu-west pool if latency acceptable
Maya L: Implemented policy to pause burst at the control plane level. Took ~2 minutes. Queue draining now slower but stops the new failed attempts
Infra Bot: policy-controller: autoscaler-burst paused for region apac at 2026-03-18T03:07:12Z by Maya L
Tony H: I ran the vendor tool on 3 nodes — two accepted KEK import and applied the new cert, one rejected with 'SecureBoot: MISMATCHED_KEYSET' — probably older BMC firmware
Leo: That explains the mixed behavior. If older BMCs can't accept the rolling key, they toggle secureboot to quarantine state and block PXE provisioning
Sara: Options: 1) Roll back BIOS to v1.11 for the rack, 2) Push BMC firmware micro-update to add Redfish key import support, 3) Manual key injection via serial for the 10% of nodes that fail
Oncall Eng: What's rollback impact? Will nodes that already accepted v1.12 stay healthy if we roll back the BIOS image?
Maya L: Rollback should restore previous keyset but takes the rack offline for ~12–18 min per node for staged rollback. Cluster capacity will be impacted. But it's safer than doing manual serial injection across many units
Tony H: Cost tradeoff: rollback duration * lost throughput vs. manual per-node ops (engineering time) + potential SLA hits if we leave them quarantined. Given the provisioning backlog and uplifted burst costs, rollback might be cheapest for customer-facing capacity
Leo: Proposed path: 1) Rollback rack-apac-3 to v1.11 during a controlled canary window (10% nodes first), 2) For nodes that still reject, schedule BMC micro-update on maintenance window, 3) Add a temporary control-plane flag to prefer eu/apac balanced placement to avoid future concentration
Sara: I'll open a Jira ticket for BMC micro-update & vendor escalation (priority P1). Add cost estimate for rollback vs manual ops
Maya L: Running canary rollback on 2 nodes now (commands: `tftp -g bios-v1.11.bin && flashrom -w bios-v1.11.bin` — per runbook). Monitoring SOL logs
Infra Bot: canary-checker: canary nodes 2/2 returned to expected secureboot state at 03:18:03Z
Oncall Eng: If canary is green, schedule rack rollback in 30min and route new provisioning requests to eu-west while we finish the job
Tony H: Also adding a mitigation: config change to control-plane to treat 'secureboot=quarantine' as provisionable for non-compliance customers only, while still blocking for enterprise customers behind private deployments
Sara: Jira created: INFRA-5421 - BMC key import failures after BIOS v1.12; vendor engaged; ETA vendor patch 72h. Link: https://redwood/internal/jira/INFRA-5421
Maya L: After rollback complete I'll run an audit script across the fleet to detect any other racks where the BIOS signed-key fingerprint changed: `python infra/tools/efi_audit.py --region apac --since 2026-03-18`
Leo: For postmortem, capture: why scheduled BIOS push didn't validate BMC Redfish key capabilities before promoting to rack, and why our canary didn't catch the key rotation (canary used only boot smoke, not secureboot fingerprint)
Oncall Eng: I'm updating the incident channel and will spin up a short postmortem doc after the rollback. Thanks all for the quick triage :thumbsup:
Sara: Ping me when rollback starts, I'll coordinate support comms and cost owner notification
Maya L: Rollback window opened at 03:49Z for rack-apac-3. I'll post updates in this thread.
Tony H: Follow-up: after rollback finished, provisioning queue dropped to 8 pending and autoscaler burst spend normalized. We'll still need to follow through on BMC firmware fixes
Leo: Adding note — add preflight that checks `GET /redfish/v1/Systems/1/SecureBoot` returns capabilities for KEK/db updates before doing any BIOS key rotations
Maya L: Noted. Closing loop here once Jira and vendor patch are in place.
